clue.text: UKIP member, for example, unconvinced by Mark's replacement?

indicators.note: 'by' here means beside, so one piece sits next to the other

blocks.note: the euro replaced the German Deutschmark as currency
someone unconvinced doubts what they are told

explanation.surface: A UKIP supporter is pictured doubting whatever replaced the German mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces come in the opposite order to the answer: the currency first, then the doubter. UKIP was a British party campaigning to leave the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A UKIP member is an example of someone hostile to the European Union and its institutions.

clue.text: At sunset proper, flower appears on medicinal plant

blocks.note: sunset comes in the evening
prim means stiffly proper
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A flower appears on a herbal plant just as the sun goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose is a herb whose seed oil is sold as a remedy, so it is a medicinal plant.

clue.text: Gunfire spasmodic around lake

indicators.note: something spasmodic jerks about irregularly, so the letters are jumbled
'around' tells us the jumbled letters wrap round another piece

blocks.note: the tail of this word, once its first three letters serve as the definition
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Bursts of gunfire are heard now and then near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word Gunfire splits in two: Gun is the definition and fire is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one particular kind of gun.

clue.text: Rescue Vatican City silver found in auction

indicators.note: things found in something are inside it, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: an auction is a kind of sale
V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Papal silverware turns up at an auction and is rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage, as a verb, means to save goods from wreck or loss, a synonym of rescue.

clue.text: Beg indulgence previously in French

indicators.note: 'previously' puts the following piece earlier, ahead of the one named before it

blocks.note: en is French for in
a treat is an indulgence

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a little indulgence, perhaps in a French lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead, a formal synonym for beg.

clue.text: Fruit going to friends who have nothing to eat

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the friends swallow the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
mates are friends
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Spare fruit is passed on to hungry friends who have nothing to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing part of the plant, though cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Clergy has old part of East Anglia embracing good state religion

indicators.note: something embracing another holds it in its arms, so it surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: the church can mean the clergy collectively
O is the abbreviation for old
the Fens are low marshy land in East Anglia
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: The clergy take over a corner of eastern England for the established faith.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the region of eastern England containing Norfolk and Suffolk, and the Fenland is its flat drained marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England is England's established church, the official religion of the state.

clue.text: Cheating by only rehearsing one key?

blocks.note: first meaning: dishonest dealing
second, playful meaning: a musician's practice confined to keys with sharps

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a sharp is a note raised a semitone, so practice in sharp keys only is sharp practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is an idiom for underhand, barely honest dealing, which is a form of cheating.

clue.text: Queen's attendant with restaurant career?

definitions.note: a whimsical description of a person, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a noblewoman serving a queen at court
second meaning, read literally: a woman whose job is waiting at tables

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey literal reading of the phrase: a lady who is in the waiting trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting is a woman of rank who personally serves a queen or princess at court.

clue.text: Man arranging duel about female is proceeding with care

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged
'about' means around, so the rearranged letters surround another piece

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A man setting up a duel over a woman is going about it cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedful means paying careful attention, which describes someone acting cautiously.

clue.text: Turned up and got together with artist for Japanese meal

indicators.note: turned round means the words that follow are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
people who got together met
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone arrived and met an artist friend over Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like the idiom for arriving, but 'Turned' is the signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Repeat service involves quarter charge

indicators.note: what involves something takes it inside, so the first word wraps the next

blocks.note: a rite is a religious service
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A service contract includes a quarterly fee, said twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say again, a more formal synonym for repeat.

clue.text: To attack youngsters is a bit shabby

indicators.note: a bit is only a part, so the answer is a piece of the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Picking on children is a rather shabby thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means cheap and in poor taste, which is close to shabby in its sense of shoddy.

clue.text: Quiet time for messenger boy

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A short break is set aside for the errand boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a boy employed in a hotel or club to carry messages and run errands.

clue.text: Agreed now to work and begin orderly life

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them busy, rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: a matter agreed is settled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to get a job and live a more regular life.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle down is an idiom for adopting a steady, quieter way of life, often with a home and job.

clue.text: Sentimental run out to island, then it''s back to club

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
the word it, its reversal signalled next
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A soppy trip: a dash to an island, then straight back to the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is run out when the ball breaks the wicket before they reach the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes someone given to tender, idealised feeling, a synonym of sentimental.

clue.text: Steward has stories to shock

indicators.note: a shock jolts and scatters things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flight attendant has some shocking tales to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: An air hostess is a female cabin crew member on an airliner, the role a flight steward plays.

clue.text: Story about Brideshead is a Universal picture

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept
'about' means around, so the story wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a tale is a story
the opening letter of the word
taken as written
U is the British film rating for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A tale about Brideshead is cast as a film from the Universal studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Brideshead Revisited is Evelyn Waugh's novel, but here the word splits into Brides and head. A U certificate in Britain means suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or group arranged like a painting, so a picture.

clue.text: To ask for money is thus legal but …

blocks.note: so means thus
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: Begging for cash is lawful, the speaker begins, before trailing off into 22.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'but …' carries the sentence on into 22 down; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to request money, custom or support, as fundraisers and charities do.

clue.text: Hamper reportedly has Greek cheese

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: to fetter is to restrain or hamper; in a non-rhotic accent it matches the cheese

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper is said to hold Greek cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white, crumbly brined cheese of sheep's or goat's milk from Greece.

clue.text: Florida city thanks politician with top award

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an A is the top grade awarded

explanation.surface: A city in Florida thanks a politician who has won a top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a major city on the Gulf coast of Florida, on Tampa Bay.

clue.text: Spanish show discord after papal decree

indicators.note: 'after' places the first piece named behind the one named later

blocks.note: a bull is a formal edict issued by the Pope
a fight is a clash of discord

explanation.surface: Spain is shown quarrelling after a pronouncement from the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfight is a traditional public spectacle in Spain in which matadors fight bulls in an arena.

clue.text: … one who gets money from wrongdoers is better!

definitions.text: one who gets money from wrongdoers

blocks.clueFragment: one who gets money from wrongdoers
blocks.note: first meaning: someone who imposes penalties in cash
second meaning: of higher quality

explanation.surface: Following 18, the one collecting penalties from offenders is the more admirable.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link back to 18 down; the first sense is a rare agent noun from the verb meaning to penalise with money.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fines is literally a finer, and finer is also the comparative of fine, meaning better.

clue.text: Fancy clothier chucked me out for a laugh

indicators.note: something fancy is elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged
chucked out means thrown away, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
I is what me becomes when the speaker is the subject

explanation.surface: A posh tailor threw the speaker out, which was rather funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh; the word was coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Hold on to last request sent in to murderer

indicators.note: 'last' keeps only the final letter of the word that follows
pieces sent in to something go inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A condemned killer is told to hang on while his final request is passed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like 'wait a moment', but only the first word is the definition and 'on' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain is to have within or keep in check, both senses of the verb hold.

clue.text: Met noble queen in need, crippled

indicators.note: something crippled is put out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order
'in' places the title and royal pieces inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
a count is a nobleman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen

explanation.surface: A lord and a queen are seen in desperate need, struck down by injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Encountered means came across or met, typically by chance.
